questions.question: Mention one limitation of pheromone-based methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Mention one limitation of pheromone-based methods.
  • Pheromones are species-specific. They may not provide immediate control of all pest stages.
  • Submerged: Hydrilla verticillata, Vallisneria.
  • Gram pod borer: Helicoverpa armigera
  • Symptoms
  • Defoliation in early stages
  • Larva’s head alone thrust inside the pods and the rest of the body hanging out.
  • Pods with round holes
  • Page 4
  • Management
  • Collection and release of potential natural enemies viz., grubs and adults of (Lady bird beetles) Coccinella
  • transversalis, Cheilo menes sexmaculatus, Harmonia octo maculata and maggots of Ischiodon scutellare.
  • Spraying of neem oil emulsion 3 % or Dimethoate 2 ml/l at the time of aphid incidence.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Spraying of neem oil emulsion 3 % or Dimethoate 2 ml/l at the time of aphid incidence.

questions.question: What is conservation of natural enemies?
questions.solution_html:
• Protection and maintenance of beneficial organisms such as predators, parasitoids and microbial
  • pathogens.These organisms naturally suppress pest populations.
  • Floating: Eichhornia crassipes (Water hyacinth),Salvinia molesta.
  • Spotted pod borer: Maruca testulalis
  • Symptoms
  • Bore holes on the buds, flower or pods
  • Infested pods and flowers are webbed together.
  • Management
  • Avoid closer plant spacing.
  • Collect and destroy larvae and adults to the extent possible
  • Install pheromone traps at a distance of 50 m
  • Collection and release of potential natural enemies.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Collection and release of potential natural enemies.

questions.question: What is a biennial weed?
questions.solution_html:
• A weed that completes its life cycle in two growing seasons. Vegetative growth occurs in the first year.Flowering
  • and seed production occurs in the second year.
  • Emergent: Typha latifolia.
  • Special Ecological Categories - Parasitic Weeds
  • Total Root Parasite: Orobanche spp. (Broomrape) on Mustard/Solanaceous crops.
  • Partial Root Parasite: Striga spp. (Witchweed) on Sorghum/Sugarcane.
  • Total Stem Parasite: Cuscuta spp. (Dodder)
  • Partial Stem Parasite: Dendrophthoe falcata (Loranthus) on fruit trees
  • Control measures
  • Cultural control: crop rotation, mulching, proper spacing and cover cropping.
  • Mechanical control: hand weeding, hoeing, tillage and mowing.
  • Physical control: heat treatment, solarization and barriers.
  • Biological control: use of natural enemies or pathogens to suppress weeds.
  • Chemical control: suitable selective or non-selective herbicides, applied according to label directions.
  • Integrated weed management combines suitable methods to reduce crop losses and environmental harm.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Integrated weed management combines suitable methods to reduce crop losses and environmental harm.

questions.question: Describe the role of plant quarantine in protecting pest-free areas.
questions.solution_html:
• Prevents introduction of pests and pathogens into pest-free areas. Regulates movement of seeds, plants and
  • planting materials. Uses inspection, testing and certification. May require treatment or destruction of infected
  • material. Protects agriculture, local ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.question: Explain the effect of insect pests on crop productivity.
questions.solution_html:
• Insect pests damage leaves, stems, roots, flowers, fruits and seeds.
  • Cause injury by chewing plant tissues or sucking sap.
  • Some insect pests transmit plant pathogens, including viruses.
  • Page 2
  • Reduce crop growth, yield and product quality.
  • Increase production costs and post-harvest losses.

questions.final_answer: Increase production costs and post-harvest losses.

questions.question: Explain the role of weed monitoring in integrated weed management.
questions.solution_html:
• Identifies weed species and estimates their abundance.
  • Determines weed distribution and level of infestation.
  • Helps to select appropriate cultural, mechanical, biological or chemical controls.
  • Enable timely control before flowering and seed production of weeds.
  • Helps to assess control effectiveness and detect possible herbicide resistance.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Helps to assess control effectiveness and detect possible herbicide resistance.

questions.question: Explain herbicide formulations.
questions.solution_html:
• Herbicide formulation combines the active herbicide ingredient with other materials to aid storage, handling and
  • application.
  • EC (Emulsifiable Concentrate): Liquid active ingredient dissolved in petroleum solvent with an emulsifier. Forms a
  • milky emulsion in water.
  • WP (Wettable Powder): Dry powder suspended in water with wetting agents. Requires continuous agitation in the
  • spray tank.
  • G / GR (Granules): Active ingredient applied onto inert granules (e.g., clay, silica). Applied directly to soil without
  • water.
  • SL (Soluble Liquid): Liquid active ingredient that completely dissolves in water to form a clear solution.
  • SC / FS (Suspension Concentrate): Solid active ingredient finely ground and suspended in a liquid base.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: SC / FS (Suspension Concentrate): Solid active ingredient finely ground and suspended in a liquid base.

questions.question: Explain the relationship between causative agent, symptoms and control.
questions.solution_html:
• Causative agent: organism or factor responsible for a disease, e.g. fungus, bacterium, virus or nutrient deficiency.
  • Symptoms: visible changes such as leaf spots, wilting, yellowing, rotting or stunting.
  • Diagnosis links symptoms with the likely cause and may require laboratory tests.
  • Control is chosen according to the cause: sanitation, resistant varieties, cultural practices or suitable
  • pesticides.Correct diagnosis is essential because different causes can produce similar symptoms.

questions.final_answer: pesticides.Correct diagnosis is essential because different causes can produce similar symptoms.

questions.question: Write a short essay on banana bunchy top disease.
questions.solution_html:
• Causal agent: Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV).
  • Vector: banana aphid, Pentalonia nigronervosa.
  • Symptoms: dark-green streaks, narrow upright leaves, shortened internodes and a bunchy appearance at the top.
  • Spread: infected planting material and viruliferous aphids.
  • Management: use disease-free planting material, remove and destroy infected plants, manage the vector and
  • follow quarantine measures.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: follow quarantine measures.

questions.question: Explain the significance of resistant host plants.
questions.solution_html:
• Resistant varieties reduce pest and disease damage.
  • Reduce dependence on chemical pesticides.
  • Can lower production costs and environmental risks.
  • Provide useful protection as part of integrated pest management.
  • Resistance may involve antixenosis (non-preference), antibiosis (adverse effect on pest) or tolerance
  • (withstanding damage).
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: (withstanding damage).

questions.question: Explain diseases due to abiotic causes.
questions.solution_html:
• Abiotic disorders arise from non-living environmental or chemical factors rather than infectious organisms.
  • Nutrient deficiencies may cause chlorosis and poor growth.
  • Water stress causes wilting; temperature extremes cause heat or chilling injury.
  • Salinity, unsuitable soil pH, poor aeration and chemical injury may damage plants.
  • Management: correct nutrient deficiencies, ensure proper irrigation and drainage, improve soil conditions and
  • avoid chemical misuse.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: avoid chemical misuse.

questions.question: Explain Integrated Pest Management (IPM). Mention the important points involved.
questions.solution_html:
• IPM combines compatible methods to keep pests below economically damaging levels while minimizing risks to
  • humans and the environment.
  • Correctly identify pests and natural enemies.
  • Page 3
  • Monitor pest populations and use economic/action thresholds where applicable.
  • Use cultural, mechanical, physical and biological methods, and resistant varieties.
  • Apply selective pesticides judiciously when needed; evaluate results and environmental safety.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Apply selective pesticides judiciously when needed; evaluate results and environmental safety.

questions.question: Explain IPM strategies with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Cultural: crop rotation, field sanitation and timely sowing.
  • Mechanical: hand-picking pests and removing infested plant parts.
  • Physical: traps, barriers and suitable heat treatments.
  • Biological: Trichogramma parasitoids or Bacillus thuringiensis against susceptible caterpillars.
  • Host resistance and need-based use of suitable selective pesticides, supported by regular monitoring.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Host resistance and need-based use of suitable selective pesticides, supported by regular monitoring.

questions.question: Discuss the weed classification and various methods of weed control.
questions.solution_html:
• Weeds are unwanted plants growing where they are not desired and competing with cultivated plants.
  • Classification by life cycle:- annual, biennial and perennial weeds.
  • Classification by morphology
  • Broadleaf Weeds (Dicots): Expanded net-veined leaves, taproot system. Examples: Parthenium hysterophorus
  • Convolvulus arvensis.
  • Grasses (Monocots): Narrow leaves with parallel veins, hollow stems with nodes, fibrous roots. Examples
  • Echinochloa, Eleusine indica.
  • Sedges (Monocots): Solid, triangular stems without nodes; 3-ranked narrow leaves. Example: Cyperus rotundus
  • Cyperus esculentus.
  • Classification by habitat
  • Terrestrial: Grown on land (dryland or irrigated fields).
  • Aquatic
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: Aquatic
